Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 91, verses 11–15 (Ash-Shams), as presented in this passage:

Surah 91 (Ash-Shams), verses 11–15: "Thamud denied (their Prophet) because of their rebellion (transgression), when the most wretched of them was sent forth..."

The story of the people of Thamud and their Prophet, Salih (peace be upon him), comes in the Qur'an in several places. We have discussed it at each of those places, and recently it passed in Surah Al-Fajr, in the same juz'. The details can be seen in those passages.

Here it is only said that the people of Thamud denied their Prophet solely because of their rebellion, and they had no other justification for it. The event was that one of them, extremely hard-hearted, rose up and slaughtered the she-camel of Allah. This man was among them so cruel and rebellious that he became ready to commit such a great crime. Yet their Prophet had warned them in clear words and had said that they should not harm this she-camel, nor interfere with the water which Allah has divided between you and the she-camel, one day for you and one day for the she-camel. This division had taken place because they had demanded a miracle from the Prophet of Allah, and so Allah made this she-camel a miracle. Some miraculous quality of this she-camel must certainly have existed. We do not go into its details here, because Allah Himself has not given the details of that aspect of its miraculous nature.

In any case, because of their rebellion they denied the one sent by Allah to warn them, and they slaughtered the she-camel. The man who actually carried out this act, having taken it upon himself, was among them exceedingly wretched and hard-hearted. But responsibility was taken by all, and all were held responsible because they did not stop that man from this evil deed but instead encouraged him. It is a fundamental principle in the teachings of Islam that in the collective life of the world, responsibility is also collective, and this law of collective responsibility does not contradict the Islamic principle of individual responsibility. That is, in the Hereafter no one will bear another's burden, and every person will have only what he has earned. Because in Islam it is also a major sin for someone to abandon advising others, to turn away from reforming others and supporting them, and not to urge people toward doing good and taking the hand of the oppressor.

When they committed this great crime, then the hand of divine power came into motion.

"So their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and levelled them (with the ground)" (Ash-Shams 91:14). The word "damdama" means wrath, and the vengeance and punishment that come as a result of wrath. The very pronunciation of the word "dam-dam" shows how severe that punishment will be. The pronunciation and rhythm of this word itself points to a terrifying scene. Allah turned their land upside down and leveled it. This is a depiction which expresses a most all-encompassing destruction.

"And He does not fear its consequence" (Ash-Shams 91:15). He is free from every weakness; how could He fear anyone? Where could He be apprehensive, and when could He be fearful?

In fact, through this manner of expression, an inherent meaning is indicated: that Allah's seizing is extremely severe, because whoever in the world does not fear any consequence commits the most severe oppression. Likewise, Allah's grip will be severe, because there is no one at all to question Allah. This is why: "Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe" (Al-Buruj 85:12). By saying that He does not fear the bad consequence of any act, the intention is to show that Allah's grip will be very severe.

Thus the human soul is connected with the great truths of this universe, and the human soul is linked with the observations and scenes of this universe. Then both the human soul and the observed universe are connected with the sunnah of Allah which He has established for seizing rebels and deniers. All these events occur within the limits of Allah's decree, in whose system Allah has fixed a time for everything. Every calamity has a fixed time. Every event has a purpose, and in this system of decree divine wisdom operates at every step. Because Allah is the Lord of the soul, the Lord of this universe, and the very manager of the system of decree and destiny. Therefore all of this lies within the scope of His vast overall design of will.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 92, verses 4–7:

ان سعیکم .................................... تردی

Your efforts are diverse. Your efforts are diverse in their reality, in their causes and motives, in their direction and aim, and in their results. The temperaments of the people who inhabit this earth are also diverse. Their thoughts and ideas are diverse, their tastes and inclinations are diverse, and their preferences are diverse. And the condition of people is such that it seems as though each one of them may be a resident of a separate planet.

This is one reality, but there is another reality that is equally present: that among all of humanity there is a common factor that binds them together, and amid all these differences there is a point of commonality. This commonality places them in two groups, keeps them standing in two rows and under two banners facing one another. What is it?

فاما ............................ بالحسنی (6:82) "So as for one who gives and fears Allah, and affirms the best [reward]" [Qur'an 92:5–6, as cited]. One is this row, and the other row.

من بخل ............................ بالحسنی (9:92) "As for one who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward]" [Qur'an 92:8–9, as cited].

There is one group that spends its life and spends its wealth, fears the punishment of Allah and the wrath of Allah, and accepts the truth; and what is the name of the truth? Al-Husna. What is its knowledge? Al-Husna. These are two kinds of people standing in two rows: people of different temperaments, different kinds of effort, different methods of action, and different aims. Lined up in these two rows, they meet one another. Each has its own system and method of conduct, and each has been granted its own particular enabling and a path given to it.

فاما ........................................ للیسری (5:95 تا 7) "So as for one who gives and fears Allah and affirms the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease" [Qur'an 92:5–7]. This is because whoever gives wealth, adopts God-consciousness, and confirms the truth has, as it were, presented what he had and made every possible effort to purify his soul and set it upon the right path. Now he deserves that Allah's help should support him and grant him the enabling of goodness, because Allah has made it incumbent upon Himself that whoever intends good, He facilitates for him; for without Allah's enabling and will, nothing can come to pass, and without it a human being can do nothing.

And whomever Allah makes facile in goodness, it is as though he has reached his destination, reached it with great ease, tranquility and peace. While on earth, he has reached the higher realm; he lives in this world with great ease. His environment and those around him become congenial to him; their steps move easily toward him, his path becomes smooth, he deals with affairs with great ease, and in short, facilities are granted to him in all generalities and particulars. This is a station and rank that encompasses everything. And one who attains this station and rank, along with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), receives great facilities, as promised.

فسنیسرہ للیسری (7:92) "We will ease him toward ease" [Qur'an 92:7].

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 92, verses 8–11:

﴿And as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship. And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into ruin].﴾ (92:8–11)

The person who is stingy with his self and his wealth, and considers himself independent of Allah, the Generous, and is heedless of His guidance, and denies the religion of Allah and His call, prepares his soul for extreme evil and corruption, and brings it to the utmost level of ruin. Such a person deserves that Allah make everything difficult for him, that the means of hardship be provided to him, and that he be enabled to face difficulties at every step. The door of ease is closed upon him, and he encounters obstacles at every step, which only take him further away from the right path and the straight way. This person keeps advancing on the path of misfortune, even though he may apparently feel that he is moving on the road to success. In reality, he keeps stumbling, and to avoid one stumble he falls into another, by which he moves even further from the straight path, so that he is deprived of the pleasure of Allah. When he advances on that deviant road filled with stumbling and at last falls into the pit of destruction, then his wealth gives him no benefit at that time, although it was this wealth that had made him independent of Allah. Now it is of no use to him.

﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into ruin].﴾ (92:11) Providing someone with facilities for evil and corruption, and enabling him to commit sin, is in reality turning him toward a difficult task and a hard path, even though such a person may appear successful in this world. The truth is that there is no more difficult destination and no more difficult abode than Hell, and here "al-'Usra" (the hardship) refers to Hell itself.

Thus ends the first paragraph of this surah, in which two paths, two methods and two systems are established for all human societies, and these two paths are for every time and place. It becomes clear that these are in reality two kings and two banners, even though their forms and colours may differ. And every person is free to choose for himself whichever path he wishes and adopt whichever method he desires. Allah provides each one with the facility that he chooses, either the path of ease or the path of hardship.

As for the next paragraph, it describes the end of each of these two parties. It shows where the one who runs and hurries will reach, the one who was granted the facility of easy paths, and where the vehicle of the one driven along hard paths will stop. In this paragraph it is told that the end of each party will be true, most just, and so it happens, and certainly it happens. For Allah showed people the right path and, if they walked on evil paths, warned them of the blazing fire.

When he advances on that deviant road filled with stumbling and at last falls into the pit of destruction, then his wealth gives him no benefit at that time, although it was this wealth that had made him independent of Allah. Now it is of no use to him.

﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into ruin].﴾ (92:11) Providing someone with facilities for evil and corruption, and enabling him to commit sin, is in reality turning him toward a difficult task and a hard path, even though such a person may appear successful in this world. The truth is that there is no more difficult destination and no more difficult abode than Hell, and here "al-'Usra" (the hardship) refers to Hell itself.

Thus ends the first paragraph of this surah, in which two paths, two methods and two systems are established for all human societies, and these two paths are for every time and place. It becomes clear that these are in reality two kings and two banners, even though their forms and colours may differ. And every person is free to choose for himself whichever path he wishes and adopt whichever method he desires. Allah provides each one with the facility that he chooses, either the path of ease or the path of hardship.

As for the next paragraph, it describes the end of each of these two parties. It shows where the one who runs and hurries will reach, the one who was granted the facility of easy paths, and where the vehicle of the one driven along hard paths will stop. In this paragraph it is told that the end of each party will be true, most just, and so it happens, and certainly it happens. For Allah showed people the right path and, if they walked on evil paths, warned them of the blazing fire.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 92, verses 8–11:

﴿And as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship. And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into ruin].﴾ (92:8–11)

The person who is stingy with his self and his wealth, and considers himself independent of Allah, the Generous, and is heedless of His guidance, and denies the religion of Allah and His call, prepares his soul for extreme evil and corruption, and brings it to the utmost level of ruin. Such a person deserves that Allah make everything difficult for him, that the means of hardship be provided to him, and that he be enabled to face difficulties at every step. The door of ease is closed upon him, and he encounters obstacles at every step, which only take him further away from the right path and the straight way. This person keeps advancing on the path of misfortune, even though he may apparently feel that he is moving on the road to success. In this paragraph it is told that the end of each party will be true, most just, and so it happens, and certainly it happens. For Allah showed people the right path and, if they walked on evil paths, warned them of the blazing fire.

God, out of His sheer grace and generosity, has made it binding upon Himself to make the path of guidance clear, both to the innate nature of people and to the faculty of perception that He has bestowed upon them. In the same way, it has been ordained for all the Messengers that they explain the Islamic call, and all the movements of invitation, all the heavenly scriptures and all the miracles were also brought for this very purpose, so that no one has any excuse left and no one suffers injustice.

﴿Indeed, upon Us is the guidance﴾ (92:12): "Indeed, it is Our responsibility to show the way." This was the first truth.

The second truth is that there is here an overpowering force (quwwat-e-qahira) which has taken all people within its grip. Against this force, people have no place of refuge.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 92, verse 13:

And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the world (13:92) ["And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first (life)"]. Therefore, where can one who wishes to be far from Allah go? There is no refuge against Him.

Keeping in view these two facts: that Allah has made it incumbent upon Himself to show the way, and that all people must then come before Allah, and that for them there is no refuge against Allah. The Master of the beginning and the end is Allah, so Allah has warned mankind that you have stood before a blazing fire.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 92, verse 14:

﴿So I have warned you of a blazing Fire.﴾ And this blazing Fire is not for everyone; rather, it is one that has been kindled.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 92, verse 15:

﴿لَا يَصْلَاهَا إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى﴾ "None will enter it except the most wretched."

And this "most wretched" is the one whose lot is the worst among all of mankind. The question arises: after being scorched by the Fire, where will he go, and a further explanation of this wretched one.

"Who denied and turned away" (92:16). That is, the Islamic call was presented to him, and he both denied it and turned away from it, although God, as He had promised, presented the call before him to guide him, and had promised that whoever comes to God with sincere desire, He would guide him to the path.

And the most God-fearing will be kept far away from it, (92:17) "The one who is most mindful of God (al-Atqa) will be kept away from it." This muttaqi (the God-conscious, one who guards against displeasure of God) is the fortunate one, in contrast to the ashqa (the most wretched).

And further explanation of this follows.

The one who gives his wealth in order to purify himself. That is, he spends his wealth so that through this spending he may become pure; the purpose of spending wealth is the purification of the wealth, not showing off or seeking greatness. He spends willingly, and he does not spend because someone had done him a favour that he wishes to repay, nor so that people may thank him. This is purely for the sake of Allah, who is his Most High Lord.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 92, verses 19–20:

"No one has a favour upon him for which he must be repaid. He gives only seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High."

What reward awaits such a person? One who is righteous (muttaqi), who spends his wealth solely for the sake of purification (tazkiyah), and who spends seeking the pleasure of his Lord, the Most High. This is the recompense and the outcome that is shown here to these pure souls. It is a very unusual reward and bounty. Departing from the customary manner, a completely new bounty is announced here.

And he will surely be well-pleased.

This pious person's heart will be filled with contentment; his soul will be filled with contentment; all his limbs will be content with what Allah has decreed; contentment will permeate every fiber of his being, and his entire life will be refreshed. How excellent is this reward, and how excellent and great a blessing it is!

"And he will surely be well-pleased" (92:21). He will be pleased with his religion, pleased with his Lord, pleased with His decree, pleased with his lot. He will be pleased with both joy and sorrow, pleased with both wealth and poverty, pleased with both ease and hardship. He will be pleased with both gentleness and harshness; he will be far from anxiety and restlessness. He will be far from distress, hastiness, heaviness and despair. In short, this contentment is a reward greater than which there is no other, and there never will be. It is a blessing for which one might spend both wealth and life. It is the one who spends his wealth so that his Lord may be pleased with him.

This is a reward that only Allah can give, and this recompense is placed into those hearts that become purely Allah's, those who see nothing but Allah.

"And he will surely be well-pleased" (92:21). He will be content, he will be happy; he gave a small price and was given much in return.

In short, at this point there is a sudden glad tidings. Indeed, the expectation of it is certainly present in the hearts of those who spend their wealth to purify it, who spend in such a way that no one has any favor over them, yet they still spend, purely for the pleasure of their Lord. Then "such a person will surely be well-pleased" (92:21).
